The main takeaway from our work is that

C. perfringes isolates are widely distributed in the gastrointestinal tract of broiler chickens and breeder hens and that the presence of C. pergringes isolates carrying the beta2-tox gene in the intestinal tract of these birds may play an important role in the pathophysiology of necrotic enterities.
C. perfrigens type A is the most prevalent in broiler chickens in Egypt and the cpbeta2 toxin gene is the most prevalent gene in the isolates.

there is a need to monitor the presence of C. per-fringens in broilers, especially the beta2-toxigenic type A strains, in order to prevent outbreaks of necrotic enteri-tis and the transmission of the disease to humans.
